sources_considered.why: CoreWeave's Q2 2025 10-Q: OpenAI agreement terms (March 2025), its liquidity statement, and loan terms tied to customer contracts.
CoreWeave release on the $2.6 billion DDTL 3.0 loan raised to deliver the OpenAI contract.
IPO prospectus (March 2025) would be ideal, but SEC returned HTTP 403.
Registration-walled; the company release covers the same facts.

evidence_items.locator: Notes to financial statements, 'Strategic Customer Agreement'

receipt.public_excerpt:
In the event of the Company’s repeated failure to meet availability of service requirements,
OpenAI has the right to terminate all or a portion of the committed amount. Under the outstanding order submitted pursuant to the Commercial Agreement, the Company has established a special
purpose vehicle that will hold the infrastructure, and the Company intends for the special purpose vehicle to incur indebtedness to finance its obligations under the Commercial Agreement.

evidence_items.explanation: The OpenAI agreement signed in March 2025 depends on CoreWeave delivering capacity, and OpenAI can terminate if CoreWeave fails. CoreWeave planned to fund the build with new debt in a special vehicle. This matches each link of the claimed chain.

metric_scope.metric: Financing plan for OpenAI contract build (new SPV debt)

receipt.public_excerpt: today announced it has closed a $2.6 billion delayed draw term loan facility (“DDTL 3.0 Facility”), continuing the company’s investment in world-class infrastructure tailored for artificial intelligence. The funding will be used to support the purchase and maintenance of advanced equipment, hardware, and cloud infrastructure systems to deliver services under a long-term agreement with OpenAI.

evidence_items.explanation: The next loan after the post was raised specifically to deliver the OpenAI contract. This shows further loans were tied to that contract and the expansion needed new debt.

metric_scope.metric: New contract-linked debt facility for expansion

receipt.public_excerpt:
We believe our existing balance of cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments, in addition to amounts available for borrowing under our various debt agreements, will be sufficient to
meet our obligations due or anticipated to be due within one year from the date of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, including operating expenses, working capital, and current commitments for
capital expenditures.

evidence_items.explanation: CoreWeave said its cash plus available borrowing covered a year of obligations, including current capex commitments. This cuts against a broad reading of 'lacks liquidity'. But it counts loans arranged after the post, and the same passage says future investments may need significant debt or equity.

metric_scope.metric: Liquidity (cash plus available borrowing) versus one-year obligations

receipt.public_excerpt:
Interest on outstanding borrowings on the DDTL 2.0 Facility accrued at a rate per annum equal to either, at our election, term SOFR or the alternative base rate plus a spread based on the credit
quality of the associated customer contracts.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows CoreWeave's existing delayed-draw loans were structured around specific customer contracts. This is background for the claim that further loans depend on contracts.
